preconditions.description: The first line of stdin is an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 30) representing the number of points to be named.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(x) <= 10**9 and 0 <= int(y) <= 10**9 for x, y in [line.split() for line in stdout.splitlines() if line.strip() and not line.strip().startswith('black') and not line.strip().startswith('white')])
preconditions.description: All printed points (x, y) must be distinct integers within bounds 0 ≤ x, y ≤ 10^9, and printed before their color is revealed.

preconditions.expression: len([line for line in stdout.splitlines() if line.strip() and not line.strip().startswith('black') and not line.strip().startswith('white')]) == n
preconditions.description: Exactly n distinct points must be printed before the line is reported.

preconditions.expression: all(line.strip() in ['black', 'white'] for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: After each point is printed, the next line of stdin is either 'black' or 'white', indicating the color of the last printed point.

postconditions.expression: all((x1*(y2 - y) + x2*(y - y1) + x*(y1 - y2)) * (x1*(y2 - y) + x2*(y - y1) + x*(y1 - y2)) > 0 for (x, y), color in zip(points, colors))
postconditions.description: The line defined by (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) must strictly separate all points into two groups: all points of one color lie on one side of the line, and all points of the other color lie on the other side. No point lies on the line.

postconditions.expression: len(points) == n and len(colors) == n and all(points[i] != points[j] for i in range(n) for j in range(i+1, n))
postconditions.description: The points and colors lists must contain exactly n distinct points and their corresponding colors, where colors are either 'black' or 'white'.

postconditions.expression: all((x1*(y2 - y) + x2*(y - y1) + x*(y1 - y2)) * (x1*(y2 - y') + x2*(y' - y1) + x'*(y1 - y2)) > 0 for (x, y), (x', y'), color, color_ in zip(points, points, colors, colors) if color != color_)
postconditions.description: For every pair of points with different colors, they must lie on opposite sides of the line defined by (x1, y1) and (x2, y2).
The line must be valid, meaning the two points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) must not coincide.
